edges.effect_quant: Randomized trials suggest the direction is more reliable than any single pooled magnitude.
edges.population: offspring of pregnant women with higher fiber intake
edges.mechanism: This early-life or prenatal exposure may shape Allergic disease through developmental programming, microbiome establishment, immune maturation, or nutrient sufficiency during sensitive windows. Timing matters because the same exposure can be much more consequential in infancy or pregnancy than later in life.
edges.summary: Maternal fiber intake during pregnancy appears tied to lower risk of allergic disease in offspring of pregnant women with higher fiber intake mainly through randomized trials. The likely magnitude is modest, which is why the edge is framed conservatively rather than as a headline-level breakthrough.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
